conn.onQuest: MemoryCard is running on this Quest: APKs install right here through the system installer.

conn.otherHeadset: You are on a different headset. To install on this one, open MemoryCard on it or use a PC.
conn.phone: You can't install on the headset from here. Open MemoryCard on a PC (sends over cable/Wi-Fi) or install the Android app on the headset itself.
conn.needAdb: To send games from the PC to the headset we use ADB (Android platform-tools, official from Google). It is downloaded once, about 7 MB.

conn.noneQuest: No headset found. Turn on Developer Mode in the Meta Horizon app, plug in the USB-C cable and accept "Allow USB debugging" on the headset.
conn.noneFrame: No headset found. On the Steam Frame, turn on Developer Mode, open "Lepton Development" in the library and connect over Wi-Fi below.

help.title: How to prepare the headset
help.q1: On your phone, Meta Horizon app > Devices > your Quest > Developer Mode: on (needs a free Meta developer account).
help.q2: Connect the Quest to the PC with a USB-C data cable and accept "Allow USB debugging" (check "Always allow").
help.q3: Installed games show up in Library > Unknown Sources. Regular Android games open in a 2D window; those that need Google Play don't work.
help.q4: No PC: install MemoryCard (APK) on the Quest and install games from it.
help.f1: On the Steam Frame: Settings > System > Developer Mode: on.
help.f2: Open "Lepton Development" in the library (the floating Android screen must be open).
help.f3: Over Wi-Fi: connect to "frame" above. Over the cable: ADB sees SteamOS; use "Connect to Lepton" (port 5555).
help.f4: Linux ARM64 builds run natively on SteamOS: download them in Desktop Mode or send them with the SteamOS Devkit Client. Quest APKs may need tweaks (the community tool FramePort does that).

flat.noteQuest: Catalog ports with an Android APK: on the Quest they open in a floating 2D window (use a Bluetooth gamepad). Apps that need Google Play are not listed.
flat.noteFrame: Android APKs run in Lepton and Linux ARM64 builds run natively on SteamOS. Linux x86 builds may run through FEX, but we haven't tested them.
